There it is reported that Carl Wolfgang Benjamin Goldschmidt was a professor of [[astronomy]] at the [[University of Göttingen]] [...] and served as an assistant to the great [[Carl Friedrich Gauss|Gauss]] at the [[observatory]] there. [...] He had long suffered from the consequences of an [[enlargement of the heart]]; and on the morning of Feb. 15, he was found in his bed, sleeping the sleep that knows no waking.}}</ref><ref name="Titan of Science">

W. B. Goldschmidt (1807–51) who discovered it (on paper) in 1831.}}</ref> '''Carl Goldschmidt''', and '''Karl Goldschmidt'''.<ref name="Mathematics of the 19th Century"/>

==Mathematical works==
A student of [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]]<ref name="Goldschmidt and Stern"/> and an assistant to Gauss at the university [[observatory]],<ref name="When Least Is Best-Bio"/><ref name="Titan of Science"/> Goldschmidt frequently collaborated with Gauss on various mathematical and scientific works. Goldschmidt was in turn a professor of Gauss's protégé [[Bernhard Riemann]].<ref name="Mathematics of the 19th Century"/> Data gathered by Gauss and Goldschmidt on the growth of the [[logarithmic integral]] compared to the [[distribution of prime numbers]] was cited by Riemann in "[[On the Number of Primes Less Than a Given Magnitude]]", Riemann's seminal paper on the [[prime-counting function]].<ref>{{cite journal | last=Riemann | first=Bernhard | title=Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse |trans-title=[[On the Number of Primes Less Than a Given Magnitude]] | language=German | journal=Monatsberichte der Königlich Preußischen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin |date=November 1859}}</ref>

In 1831, Goldschmidt wrote a mathematical treatise in [[Latin language|Latin]], "Determinatio superficiei minimae rotatione curvae data duo puncta jungentis circa datum axem ortae" ("Determination of the surface-minimal rotation curve given two joined points about a given axis of origin").<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bPs-AAAAYAAJ | title=Bibliographic Information: Determinatio superficiei minimae rotatione curvae data duo puncta jungentis circa datum axem ortae | access-date=2012-08-27| year=1831 | last1=Goldschmidt | first1=Benjamin }}</ref> The paper dealt with the problem in the [[calculus of variations]] of determining the [[minimal surface of revolution]], the [[surface of revolution]] of the [[plane (geometry)|planar]] [[curve]] between two given [[point (geometry)|points]] which [[mathematical optimization|minimizes]] [[surface area]].<ref name="Mathworld: Minimal Surface of Revolution">{{cite web | url=http://mathworld.wolfram.com/MinimalSurfaceofRevolution.html | title=Minimal Surface of Revolution | last=Weisstein | first=Eric W. | author-link=Eric W. Weisstein | work=[[Mathworld]] | publisher=[[Wolfram Research]] | access-date=2012-08-29}}</ref> [[equation solving|Solutions]] to the problem exist which are not [[continuous function|continuous]]; such [[discontinuous]] solutions are known as [[Goldschmidt solutions]] in honor of Goldschmidt's discovery of them.<ref name="When Least Is Best-Solution"/><ref name="Mathworld: Goldschmidt Solution">{{cite web | url=http://mathworld.wolfram.com/GoldschmidtSolution.html | title=Goldschmidt Solution | last=Weisstein | first=Eric W. | author-link=Eric W. Weisstein | work=[[Mathworld]] | publisher=[[Wolfram Research]] | access-date=2012-08-29}}</ref>

==Physics works==
In 1834, Goldschmidt co-authored, in German, the textbook ''Lehrbuch der analytischen Optik'' (''Textbook of Analytical [[Optics]]'') with J. C. Eduard Schmidt.<ref name="Google Books: Lehrbuch"/> Together with Gauss and [[Wilhelm Eduard Weber]], Goldschmidt published in 1840 ''Atlas des Erdmagnetismus: nach den Elementen der Theorie entworfen'' (''[[Atlas]] of [[Geomagnetism]]: According to the Elements of the Theory of Design''), a series of [[magnetism|magnetic]] [[map]]s.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://archive.org/details/atlasdeserdmagn00gausgoog | title=Book Details Page: Atlas Des Erdmagnetismus: Nach Den Elementen Der Theorie Entworfen | publisher=World Ebook Fair | access-date=2012-08-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | url=http://www.alibris.com/booksearch?qwork=-587234182 | title=Atlas Des Erdmagnetismus: Nach Den Elementen Der Theorie Entworfen | publisher=Alibris | access-date=2012-08-27}}</ref> In 1845, Goldschmidt published, also in German, a book on [[electromagnetism]], ''Untersuchungen über die magnetische Declination in Göttingen'' (''Studies of the [[magnetic declination|Magnetic Declination]] in [[Göttingen]]'').<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gD0aMAEACAAJ | title=Bibliographic Information: Untersuchungen über die magnetische Declination in Göttingen | access-date=2012-08-27}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Goldschmidt, who suffered from an [[enlargement of the heart]], died in his sleep and was found on the morning of 15 February 1851.<ref name="When Least Is Best-Bio" /><ref name="Titan of Science" />
